tasks.short: Recognise an urgent security issue, call the police by phone or radio, secure the area until they arrive, and log the call.

steps.what: Security screener recognises an urgent security issue and decides to call the police
Security screener contacts police directly using phones or two-way radios
Security screener secures the area until the police arrive
Security screener writes the time and reason of the police call in the checkpoint log

tasks.design: Police calls are logged on the checkpoint terminal ({OTHER}) with one entry that stamps time and lane and offers a list of reasons, instead of writing them in a paper log afterwards. Recognising the issue, calling the police and securing the area stay with the screener.
tasks.previous_blocker: Police calls were written in a paper log after the event.
tasks.enabler_now: Checkpoint terminals can stamp and log events per lane.
tasks.still_hard: During an incident there is no time to log.
tasks.human_edge: Staying calm and keeping passengers away while police are on their way.

reach.learn: Whether police calls are logged completely.

evidence.claim: Checkpoint terminals can log events with time and lane stamped.
Logs that record which screener did what can observe staff and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the incident at the checkpoint to the call logged; police handling is outside.
Input contract: terminals at each lane; fallback is the paper log.
Recognising, calling and securing keep their full time. s4 keeps 75 because time and lane are stamped and the screener still records the reason and what happened.

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: completing the log entry after the incident is s4 itself.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the terminal is often busy during the incident, so most calls are logged afterwards with the time typed (1.0); high: calls logged at the terminal as designed (2.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the alarm details from the scanner, write bag, flight and alarm details in the alarm log, add the search outcome, and hand the log to the supervisor.

steps.what: Security screener reads the alarm details from the scanner screen
Security screener records information about baggage that sets off alarms in the paper alarm log
Security screener adds the outcome of the bag search to the log: written in the paper log today, picked from a list with a short note after the change
Security screener hands the alarm log to the supervisor at the end of the shift

tasks.design: On lanes where the scanner is linked to the alarm log ({OTHER}), about 80%, an alarm creates a log entry with the bag tag, lane, time, alarm type and image reference filled in, so the screener does not read and copy them; the screener records the outcome from a list with a short note, in about the time it takes on paper. The supervisor sees entries as they are made, so no paper log is handed in. Older lanes keep the paper log.
tasks.previous_blocker: Alarm details were copied from the screen into a paper log.
tasks.enabler_now: Linked scanners can create alarm records with details filled in.
tasks.still_hard: Older scanners have no data link.
tasks.human_edge: Recording an unusual item so the next shift knows what to look for.
tasks.altitude: The screener records outcomes instead of copying details.

evidence.claim: Linked baggage scanners can create alarm records with bag tag, time and image reference filled in.
Records linking bags to passengers are personal data and are kept only as long as needed.

assumptions: Boundary: from the bag alarm to the log handed in; searching the bag is outside.
Input contract: linked scanners on most lanes; fallback is the paper log.
Scenario: about 80% of lanes have scanners linked to the alarm log.
Recording the outcome is a first record and keeps its full time. s2 keeps 45 for older lanes and for checking filled entries; s4 keeps 20 for paper logs from older lanes.

incremental.description: Security screener corrects entries linked to the wrong bag.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only about half of the lanes are linked, so more alarms are copied by hand and paper logs handed in (27.2); high: about 80% of lanes linked as assumed (43.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study posted pictures at shift start, watch passengers for potentially dangerous persons, report a possible match, and sign that new pictures were read.

steps.what: Security screener studies the pictures posted at the checkpoint at shift start
Security screener watches for potentially dangerous persons whose pictures are posted
Security screener reports a possible match to the supervisor
Security screener confirms that new pictures were read: by signing a paper list today, by a tap on the terminal after the change

tasks.design: The checkpoint terminal ({OTHER}) shows the current pictures at shift start with new ones marked, so the screener does not search the board for changes, and the screener taps to confirm they were read instead of signing a paper list, which takes as long. No face recognition is used; watching passengers and reporting a match stay with the screener.
tasks.previous_blocker: Pictures were pinned on a board and reading was signed on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Checkpoint terminals can show briefing material and record read confirmations.
tasks.still_hard: Pictures are often old or of poor quality.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a face despite a changed haircut and glasses.

reach.learn: Whether all screeners saw new pictures.

evidence.claim: Checkpoint terminals can show briefing pictures and record read confirmations.
Real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement is banned with narrow exceptions; none is used here.

assumptions: Boundary: from the shift start to the match reported; police action is outside.
Input contract: pictures loaded by the security office; fallback is the board.
Watching passengers, reporting and confirming the reading keep their full time; confirming is sized at 4 because it takes seconds. s1 keeps 70 because new pictures are marked and studying them stays.
research_questions: Do all screeners see new pictures before their shift?

incremental.description: Security screener reports pictures that do not load.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few pictures change between shifts, so little search time is saved (1.7); high: frequent updates (4.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Judge that an object is of concern, look it up in the prohibited items list, discuss it with the lead or supervisor, and note the object and decision.

steps.what: Security screener judges that an object is of concern
Security screener looks up the object in the prohibited items binder
Security screener contacts the lead or supervisor to discuss objects of concern not on the prohibited list
Security screener notes the object and decision: on paper today, in the terminal log with a category and photo after the change

tasks.design: The prohibited items list is searchable with pictures on the checkpoint terminal ({OTHER}), so the screener does not leaf through a binder, and earlier decisions on similar objects show beside it. The screener logs the object and decision on the same terminal with a category and photo instead of on paper; this first record keeps its time. Judging the object and discussing it with the lead stay with the screener.
tasks.previous_blocker: The list was in a binder and decisions were written on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Checkpoint terminals can search item lists and log decisions with photos.
tasks.still_hard: New kinds of objects have no earlier decision.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing why a passenger carries an odd object.

evidence.claim: Checkpoint terminals can search item lists with pictures and log decisions with photos.
Logs that record which screener did what can observe staff and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the object found to the decision logged; confiscation procedures are outside.
Input contract: list and pictures kept by the security office; fallback is the binder.
Judging, discussing with the lead and logging the decision (a first record) keep their full time. s2 keeps 40 because the list is searched with pictures and reading it stays.
research_questions: Do decisions on similar objects become more consistent?

incremental.description: Security screener adds photos of new objects.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many objects of concern are not in the list, so the search helps less (4.0); high: most objects are found in the list (8.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The security screener keeps judging objects and people, calling police and discussing with leads; paper logs, binders and copied alarm details shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A screener with more attention on passengers.
